chunks: Until, when he reached the setting of the sun, he saw it set in a muddy spring, and he found near it a people. We said: 'O Dhu al-Qarnain, either you punish [them] or else take from them kindness.'

key_terms.ذُو الْقَرْنَيْنِ: Dhu al-Qarnain (The Two-Horned One), a righteous prophet-king
key_terms.قُلْنَا: We said, indicating divine address to the prophet
key_terms.مَغْرِبَ الشَّمْسِ: The setting of the sun, referring to the western extremity of the earth

ai.seo_question: What did Dhu al-Qarnain see when he reached the setting of the sun?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'muddy spring' (ayn hamiah) is often interpreted either literally as the western horizon or symbolically as a place of ignorance, highlighting Dhu al-Qarnain’s role as a just ruler who administers divine justice based on the faith of the people. This encounter underscores the principle of *amr bi-l-ma'ruf wa nahy an al-munkar* (commanding good and forbidding evil), where his governance is contingent upon the moral state of the community. The verse establishes a paradigm for leadership that balances mercy and authority, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imam's dual role as both spiritual guide and temporal administrator.
